name: Greenhouse & Nursery Production

objectives.text: Identify a greenhouse and describe why plants grow well inside it
Identify the needs of a potted plant such as light, water, air, warmth, and growing media
Describe how a greenhouse lets in light and traps heat to control the growing environment
Sow seeds in flats or plug trays and record germination and seedling growth over time
Explain how greenhouse glazing, ventilation, shading, and heating systems maintain a controlled environment
Distinguish greenhouse crops from nursery crops such as bedding plants, potted flowers, shrubs, and shade trees
Propagate plants from stem and leaf cuttings and describe the conditions that promote rooting
Demonstrate proper potting, transplanting, and spacing techniques for greenhouse and nursery stock
Describe the major forms of growing media used in greenhouse and nursery production and explain why media is prepared before planting
Identify greenhouse and nursery plants by their purpose such as floral, bedding, foliage, and landscape plants
Explain the effects of temperature, humidity, air movement, and light on crop germination, growth, and development in a greenhouse
Describe greenhouse structures, coverings, and technologies used for controlled environment production
Analyze environmental control systems for temperature, humidity, carbon dioxide, and light used in commercial greenhouse production
Calculate fertilizer injector ratios and monitor substrate pH and electrical conductivity to manage irrigation and fertigation
Apply photoperiod control and plant growth regulators to manage flowering and plant height in greenhouse crops
Explain nursery production systems including container, pot-in-pot, and field-grown balled and burlapped stock along with hardening off and overwintering
Recommend a plan for managing crop growth in different growing media including soilless mixes and hydroponic systems
Prepare a scouting report that diagnoses environmental and nutritional problems in a greenhouse crop and recommends corrections
Evaluate a plan to maintain optimal day length, light, humidity, moisture, and temperature for a specific greenhouse crop
Create a greenhouse production schedule from propagation to finish that times a crop for a market date such as Mother's Day
Grade and prepare finished greenhouse and nursery plants for sale according to industry standards for size and quality
Evaluate the energy use, sustainability, and local market impact of greenhouse production compared with shipped-in plant products
Design a greenhouse or nursery SAE enterprise with a crop plan, budget, and record-keeping system

changes: Kept and lightly reworded all six existing objectives, rewording the grade 12 scheduling objective to center on creating a market-timed production schedule. Added objectives for plant needs, seed sowing, crop types, cutting propagation, growing media, environmental effects on growth, greenhouse structures, fertigation with pH and EC monitoring, photoperiod and growth regulators, nursery production systems, media management plans, environmental scouting, evaluating environmental plans, grading for sale, sustainability, and SAE enterprise design. Pest management, fruit and vegetable crops, and field crops were left to sibling sub-topics. AFNR codes were attached only at grades 9 to 12 where the objective teaches the standard.
